summary: An Instagram story read now bounds every value it hands to the model, not just the field names, and says «I don't know whose account» instead of «there's nothing there».
details: A note written by either social bridge is dropped rather than forwarded: it landed in the slot that tells Nora what she may say, and an injected sentence in it reached the model intact.

A story frame's media link must resolve to a measured Instagram CDN host, and its id must look like an id — https alone and str() of whatever arrived were both content channels wearing a reference field's name.
A malformed first frame no longer hides a good second one: rows are dropped before the limit is applied, so «read my latest story» still answers when frame one is unreadable.
The rendered story text is now wrapped as stranger-written and clamped, the same as every other social read; the machine-usable link stays unescaped in the items list.
A story target that is not a person id answers «ambiguous» — I don't know which account that is, so I didn't look — instead of claiming the read ran and found nothing.
limitations: The Instagram story backend is still unwired in production: it needs the person index to carry Instagram ids, so the tool answers «I couldn't check» until then.
